entries.admissibility_component: L determines admissible/inadmissible continuation gating before orientation is evaluated.
entries.orientation_component: Q specifies local orientation relation among admissible continuation candidates.
entries.precedence_rule: L precedes Q: orientation cannot be evaluated as valid until admissibility has first constrained the candidate continuation.
entries.composition_rule: O=(L,Q) composition is valid only when the output admissibility state of the first operator is compatible with the input admissibility state of the next.
entries.degeneracy_rule: If multiple O candidates minimize relational mismatch equally, O* is set-valued and induces a set-valued -(i) equivalence class.
entries.relation_to_minus_i: -(i) is the local admissibility reference induced by O* through Ref(.), not O* itself.
remaining_gaps: full composition table for O_i ∘ O_j
identity element or neutral operator condition

identity_conditions.name: admissibility_identity_v1
identity_conditions.statement: An O composition acts as identity when it preserves admissibility status, induced Ref(.) equivalence class, and transition legality.

identity_conditions.name: orientation_identity_v1
identity_conditions.statement: An orientation component acts as identity relative to a local equivalence class when it induces the same -(i) under Ref(.).

entries.admissibility_component: Historical residue R deforms the local admissibility window, narrowing or shifting the domain of allowed continuations.
entries.orientation_component: Residue trace provides the directional bias for orientation selection among admissible candidates.
entries.precedence_rule: R(t-1) deforms the window for Δ(t); the selection event at t then updates R(t).
entries.composition_rule: Residue accumulation behaves as a recursive ratchet; operators compose via historical convolution.
entries.degeneracy_rule: When multiple residues yield equal mismatch, the system enters a multi-valued history state until a symmetry-breaking selection occurs.
entries.relation_to_minus_i: The residue history is the encoded -(i) sequence that determines future admissibility geometry.
remaining_gaps: residue decay rates vs. reinforcement rates
saturation limits of the admissibility ratchet

identity_conditions.name: residue_neutrality_v1
identity_conditions.statement: An update is residue-neutral if it leaves the historical admissibility trace unchanged.

entries.admissibility_component: Additive perturbation δ generates distinguishability pressure required to cross the θ threshold.
entries.orientation_component: δ specifies the relational asymmetry that guides orientation selection.
entries.precedence_rule: δ must exceed θ before admissibility selection can occur.
entries.composition_rule: Deviation-conditioned operators compose via additive distinguishability increments.
entries.degeneracy_rule: Degeneracy occurs when δ < θ, resulting in unresolved distinction (coherence).
entries.relation_to_minus_i: δ generates the relational distance from the local -(i) reference.
remaining_gaps: relationship between δ and update magnitude Δ

identity_conditions.name: sub_threshold_invariance_v1
identity_conditions.statement: An update is deviation-invariant if it fails to cross the distinguishability threshold θ.

entries.admissibility_component: Relative phase coherence ϕ determines the degree of relational coupling and interaction reach.
entries.orientation_component: ϕ specifies the local phase relation used for synchronization-based selection.
entries.precedence_rule: Phase coherence determines the interaction domain (K) before orientation alignment is evaluated.
entries.composition_rule: Phase-conditioned operators compose via relational synchronization dynamics.
entries.degeneracy_rule: Degeneracy occurs in zero-phase-gradient regions where no local orientation is distinguished.
entries.relation_to_minus_i: The phase gradient induces the local -(i) orientation frame.

identity_conditions.name: synchronization_identity_v1
identity_conditions.statement: An update acts as phase-identity when it maintains perfect relational coherence.
